g.text: Settings | Global preferences, appearance, storage, and app behavior | Local
State: Draft — save with s | Changes affect global Console fallbacks after save.
Limits on ONE agent run (one message you send). Raise them for long, expensive
sessions. The token budget is what normally stops a long run - the turn and step
limits are backstops. Sub-agents inherit these, so a run that spawns helpers can
spend several times the token budget.
The limit that actually stops a long run. Counts prompt + completion for ONE run
(one message), not the whole conversation - and the whole conversation is re-sent
every turn, so spend grows quadratically: 25M is typically reached around turn
250. Sub-agents each get this same ceiling rather than a share of it, so one
message's worst case is about 3x it. 0 = unlimited. Loop detection stops
identical repeated calls and 3 consecutive failures from the same tool;
successful calls with changing arguments can still loop.
= 2m. How long ONE run may take end to end. Stop works throughout. Sub-agents are
child_max_wall_seconds, so raising this does not extend
0 = unlimited. Ceiling on a SINGLE tool call - the real limit on long crawls,
ingests, and builds, which a large wall-clock budget alone will not save. 0 = no
ceiling (Stop still works: it is polled every 0.5s while a tool runs). A call
reported as timed out may still finish later on its own thread, so lowering this
below ~186s can double-execute an MCP tool.
Tool-calling rounds per message. A backstop, not the usual limiter - at the
default token budget a run stops on spend first, long before this.
Individual loop steps. One tool round costs 3 (think, call, result) and the
closing reply costs 1, so N turns need 3*(N-1)+1 steps. Set below that and this,
not the turn count, becomes your limiter. Maximum supported: 199,999 steps.
Note: 400 steps caps this run at about 134 tool-calling rounds, not 200 - a tool
round costs 3 steps, so 200 turns need 598. The step backstop will stop runs
How much of an agent tool result the Console shows you here -- distinct from
Esc, s save category | Esc, r revert category | F1 help · F6 next pane · Ctrl+P palette · Ctrl+Q quit
